competitors.title: JetBrains Junie Leaves Beta: GA Release Features (June 2026)
key_points: Junie moved out of beta on June 17, 2026 — same day Vercel launched eve
Three major GA additions: agentic debugging, standalone CLI, bring-your-own-model keys
Agentic debugging: autonomous breakpoint setting, step-through execution, variable inspection, runtime state reasoning using IDE's own debugger
Standalone CLI works in terminal, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI — direct response to Claude Code and Codex CLI
BYO model keys: Anthropic (Claude Opus 4.8/Fable 5/Sonnet), OpenAI (GPT-5.5/5.4), Google (Gemini 3.5 Pro)
Deep semantic codebase index from JetBrains' 25-year IDE infrastructure — compiler-grade vs Cursor's text-and-embedding approach
Pricing unchanged: AI Pro $100/yr (10 credits/mo), AI Ultimate $300/yr (35 credits/mo)
Heavy debugging session can consume 1-3 credits per task; $80 of Ultimate credits can exhaust in a single day on large projects
Decision matrix: Junie for JetBrains-native deep analysis, Cursor 4 for VS Code/best UX, Claude Code for terminal-first
Junie CLI is the more strategic move — lets JetBrains compete in CI/CD and terminal markets

competitors.title: JetBrains AI Plans & Pricing
key_points: AI Pro: $100/year (~$8.33/mo), 10 AI credits per 30 days — designed for regular AI-enhanced IDE workflows with occasional agent use
AI Ultimate: $300/year (~$25/mo), 35 AI credits per 30 days — maximum credits, enterprise security, custom AI integrations
All-Apps + AI add-on: ~$10/mo, ~3 credits — commit descriptions only, too small for agentic work
Yearly billing saves 2 months vs monthly
BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) option available for cost control and data residency
Enterprise: AI for Business with fine-grained control over AI tools
